items.stem: Which control sits highest in the hierarchy of controls for a hazardous solvent?

options.text: Eliminate the solvent by redesigning the process to not need it
options.rationale: Correct: elimination is the most effective, highest-order control.
PPE is the lowest-order control, used last.
Signage is an administrative control, lower than elimination.
Procedures are administrative controls, below elimination and substitution.

items.explanation: Correct: elimination is the most effective, highest-order control.

items.stem: A risk rating uses likelihood and severity. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Raising either likelihood or severity raises the risk rating
options.rationale: Correct: risk is a function of both factors.

options.text: A low-likelihood but catastrophic event can still rate as high risk
options.rationale: Correct: high severity can drive a high rating despite low likelihood.

options.text: Only likelihood determines the risk rating
options.rationale: Severity is equally part of the rating.

options.text: Severity is irrelevant once likelihood is known
options.rationale: Severity is essential to the rating.

items.explanation: Correct: risk is a function of both factors.

items.stem: An incident investigation concludes 'the worker was careless'. Why is this inadequate?

options.text: It stops at individual blame and ignores system causes that could prevent recurrence
options.rationale: Correct: effective investigation finds systemic causes and preventive actions.

options.text: It is the ideal root cause for most incidents
options.rationale: Individual blame is rarely the true root cause and prevents learning.
Blame alone yields no preventive action.

options.text: It removes the need for corrective action
options.rationale: Corrective and preventive action are still required.

items.explanation: Correct: effective investigation finds systemic causes and preventive actions.
